title: Measurement compatibility, dilation and identifiable tomography

items.title: Finite Hermitian frames and their Gram pseudoinverse
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
For an integer $d\ge1$, let $\mathsf H_d=\{A\in M_d(\mathbb C):A=A^*\}$, regarded as a real vector space. For $A,B\in\mathsf H_d$, define the trace pairing $\langle A,B\rangle_{\mathrm{HS}}:=\operatorname{Tr}(AB)$ and write $\|A\|_{\mathrm{HS}}:=\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(A^2)}$. The following A-page lemma verifies that the pairing is a real inner product and that this expression is its norm.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $F=(F_a)_{a=1}^m$ be a finite family in $\mathsf H_d$. It is informationally complete when its real linear span is all of $\mathsf H_d$. Its synthesis map is $S:\mathbb R^m\to\mathsf H_d$, $S c=\sum_{a=1}^m c_aF_a$. Define the Gram matrix by $G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Tr}(F_aF_b)$.

Equip $\mathbb R^m$ with the dot product $c^\mathsf Tb=\sum_{a=1}^m c_ab_a$. Here $S^*:\mathsf H_d\to\mathbb R^m$ denotes the adjoint relative to this dot product and the displayed trace pairing: it is characterized by $c^\mathsf T(S^*X)=\langle Sc,X\rangle_{\mathrm{HS}}$ for every $c\in\mathbb R^m$ and $X\in\mathsf H_d$. The following lemma proves that the trace pairing is an inner product and that this adjoint exists as a well-defined linear map; it also establishes that $G=S^*S$ is real symmetric positive semidefinite.

For this positive semidefinite real matrix $G$, let $G^+$ be its unique Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse in $M_m(\mathbb R)$, defined by the four Penrose equations over $\mathbb R$. Define the canonical dual operators $D_a=\sum_{b=1}^m(G^+)_{ba}F_b$ and the reconstruction map $D:\mathbb R^m\to\mathsf H_d$, $D c=\sum_{a=1}^m c_aD_a$. A later A-page lemma identifies this finite pseudoinverse with its spectral formula.

references.title: Xhek Turkeshi and Markus Heinrich, Quantum Information Methods for Many-Body Physics, §3.1
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.2

items.title: Two-sided Hoeffding bound for Bernoulli frequencies
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $p\in[0,1]$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n:\Omega\to\{0,1\}$ be measurable on a probability space with
$$\mathbb P(X_1=x_1,\ldots,X_n=x_n)=\prod_{k=1}^n b_p(x_k)\quad\text{for every }(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\{0,1\}^n.$$
Here $b_p(1)=p$ and $b_p(0)=1-p$, including $p=0$ and $p=1$. Thus the variables have the stated independent Bernoulli product law. For their frequency $f=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^nX_k$ and every $t>0$,
$$
\mathbb P(|f-p|\ge t)\le2e^{-2nt^2}.
$$
No axiom of choice is assumed.

references.title: Dmitry Panchenko, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.465, Lecture 07: Hoeffding’s inequality, Spring 2007

items.title: Finite instrument dilation with an outcome register
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d,e\ge1$ and let $\mathcal A$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A finite completely positive instrument from $\mathbb C^d$ to $\mathbb C^e$ is a family of completely positive complex-linear maps $I_a:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_e(\mathbb C)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal A$, whose sum is trace-preserving. Then there are an integer $q\ge1$, an isometry $V:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^e\otimes\mathbb C^q$, and pairwise orthogonal projections $Q_a$ on $\mathbb C^q$ with $\sum_aQ_a=I_q$ such that, for every $X\in M_d(\mathbb C)$,
$$
I_a(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E\!\left[(I_e\otimes Q_a)VXV^*(I_e\otimes Q_a)\right].
$$
Here $E=\mathbb C^q$ is the finite register space with its displayed orthonormal basis, and the partial trace is defined on its matrix units by $\operatorname{Tr}_E(Y\otimes|e_{a,r}\rangle\langle e_{b,s}|)=\delta_{(a,r),(b,s)}Y$, extended linearly. The register basis is indexed by the Kraus labels $(a,r)$; a zero outcome map has no labels and corresponds to $Q_a=0$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §2.2.2, Theorem 2.22
Richard Cleve, Quantum Information Processing, QIC 710 course notes, Fall 2023, §§3.3–3.5

items.title: Sharp finite joint measurability forces commutation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $I,J$ be finite nonempty sets, and let $(P_i)_{i\in I}$ and $(Q_j)_{j\in J}$ be projection-valued measures: $P_i=P_i^*=P_i^2$, $Q_j=Q_j^*=Q_j^2$, distinct projections in each family are orthogonal, and $\sum_iP_i=\sum_jQ_j=I_H$. A joint POVM is a family of effects $(G_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$ with $\sum_{i,j}G_{ij}=I_H$, $\sum_jG_{ij}=P_i$, and $\sum_iG_{ij}=Q_j$. Such a joint POVM exists exactly when $P_iQ_j=Q_jP_i$ for every $i,j$. When it exists it is unique and equals $G_{ij}=P_iQ_j$.

references.title: Teiko Heinosaari, Daniel Reitzner, and Peter Stano, Notes on Joint Measurability of Quantum Observables, §2 and Appendix, Proposition 8
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §2.1.3

items.title: The real trace pairing on finite Hermitian matrices is an inner product
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Let $\mathsf H_d$ be the real vector space of Hermitian $d\times d$ complex matrices from the preceding definition. The pairing $\langle A,B\rangle_{\mathrm{HS}}=\operatorname{Tr}(AB)$ is real-valued, symmetric, real-bilinear, and positive definite on $\mathsf H_d$. Its associated norm is $\|A\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(A^2)}$. For every $m\ge1$ and finite family $F_1,\ldots,F_m\in\mathsf H_d$, the Gram matrix $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}(F_aF_b)$ is real symmetric positive semidefinite, equals $S^*S$ for the synthesis map $S c=\sum_ac_aF_a$, and satisfies $\ker G=\ker S$.

references.title: Xhek Turkeshi and Markus Heinrich, Quantum Information Methods for Many-Body Physics, §3.1, equation (3.2)

items.title: Informationally complete linear tomography
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Input integers $d,m\ge1$, a finite POVM $(F_a)_{a=1}^m$ on $\mathbb C^d$ that spans the real Hermitian matrices, and real frequencies $f_a\ge0$ with $\sum_af_a=1$. Form the Gram matrix $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}(F_aF_b)$, compute its Moore–Penrose inverse $G^+$, set $D_a=\sum_b(G^+)_{ba}F_b$, and return
$$
X=\sum_{a=1}^m f_aD_a.
$$
All sums and matrices are finite. The output is Hermitian. The procedure does not project $X$ onto the positive cone, and it makes no positivity claim for finite frequency inputs.

references.title: Xhek Turkeshi and Markus Heinrich, Quantum Information Methods for Many-Body Physics, §3.1, equations (3.7)–(3.9)

items.title: The Gram pseudoinverse reconstructs a spanning Hermitian frame
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d,m\ge1$, let $F_1,\ldots,F_m\in\mathsf H_d$ span $\mathsf H_d$ over $\mathbb R$, and form $S$, $G=S^*S$, $G^+$, and $D_a$ as in the preceding finite-frame definition. If $G=\sum_{\lambda>0}\lambda P_\lambda$ is its finite spectral resolution, then $G^+=\sum_{\lambda>0}\lambda^{-1}P_\lambda$. Moreover, every $X\in\mathsf H_d$ is reconstructed by
$$
X=\sum_{a=1}^m\operatorname{Tr}(XF_a)D_a.
$$
This holds for redundant families as well as bases; $G$ need not be invertible.

references.title: Xhek Turkeshi and Markus Heinrich, Quantum Information Methods for Many-Body Physics, §3.1, linear inversion
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §2.1

items.title: Tomography correctness and finite-sample stability
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d,m,n\ge1$, let $(F_a)_{a=1}^m$ be a finite POVM on $\mathbb C^d$ whose real span is $\mathsf H_d$, and let $\rho\in\mathsf H_d$ satisfy $\rho\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Put $p_a=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho F_a)$, form the canonical dual $D_a$ from the Gram pseudoinverse, and write $D:\mathbb R^m\to\mathsf H_d$ for $D c=\sum_ac_aD_a$.

Define the frequency simplex $\Delta_m=\{f\in\mathbb R^m:f_a\ge0\text{ for all }a,\ \sum_af_a=1\}$ and the real-linear map $X:\mathbb R^m\to\mathsf H_d$ by $X(f)=\sum_af_aD_a$. On $\Delta_m$, this is the output of the previously defined linear-inversion procedure; on all of $\mathbb R^m$, $X$ denotes its linear extension. Use the induced operator norm $\|D\|_{2\to\mathrm{HS}}=\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\|Dc\|_{\mathrm{HS}}$.

Then exact probabilities reconstruct the state: $X(p)=\rho$. For every real frequency vector $f\in\mathbb R^m$,
$$
\|X(f)-\rho\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\|D\|_{2\to\mathrm{HS}}\|f-p\|_2.
$$
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space and let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n:\Omega\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$ be measurable with the independent product law $\mathbb P(Y_1=a_1,\ldots,Y_n=a_n)=\prod_kp_{a_k}$ for every outcome tuple. Define $f_a=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n\mathbf1_{\{Y_k=a\}}$. Then for every $0<\delta<1$,
$$
\mathbb P\!\left(\max_{1\le a\le m}|f_a-p_a|\le\sqrt{\frac{\log(2m/\delta)}{2n}}\right)\ge1-\delta.
$$
Consequently, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$$
\|X(f)-\rho\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\|D\|_{2\to\mathrm{HS}}\sqrt m\sqrt{\frac{\log(2m/\delta)}{2n}}.
$$
These are conditional mathematical statements under the specified product sampling law; no empirical data or calibrated apparatus is asserted.

references.title: Xhek Turkeshi and Markus Heinrich, Quantum Information Methods for Many-Body Physics, §3.1, equations (3.7)–(3.9)
Dmitry Panchenko, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.465, Lecture 07: Hoeffding’s inequality, Spring 2007

items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: For finite quantum instruments on $\mathbb C^2$, equality of all outcome effects forces equality of the outcome update maps on every input matrix.

items.title: Pauli six-outcome tomography
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
On $\mathbb C^2$, define the Pauli matrices
$$
\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \sigma_y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Let $I=I_2$, let $\mathsf H_2=\{A\in M_2(\mathbb C):A=A^*\}$, and let $\operatorname{Tr}$ denote the diagonal-sum trace. For $v\in\mathbb C^2$, write $v^*=\bar v^{\mathsf T}$. For $A\in M_2(\mathbb C)$, $A\ge0$ means $A=A^*$ and $v^*Av\ge0$ for every $v\in\mathbb C^2$. A finite POVM is a finite family of positive semidefinite matrices whose sum is $I$; it is informationally complete when its real linear span is $\mathsf H_2$. The six matrices $F_{j,\pm}=(I\pm\sigma_j)/6$, with $j\in\{x,y,z\}$, form such an informationally complete POVM. For every $\rho\in M_2(\mathbb C)$ with $\rho\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, there are unique $r_x,r_y,r_z\in\mathbb R$ such that $\rho=(I+r_x\sigma_x+r_y\sigma_y+r_z\sigma_z)/2$. Define $p_{j,\pm}:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho F_{j,\pm})$; then $r_j=3(p_{j,+}-p_{j,-})$. Form $G_{(j,s),(k,t)}=\operatorname{Tr}(F_{j,s}F_{k,t})$ and the canonical duals $D_{j,s}=\sum_{k,t}(G^+)_{(k,t),(j,s)}F_{k,t}$ as in the preceding finite-frame definition. The linear-inversion procedure returns $X(f)=\sum_{j,s}f_{j,s}D_{j,s}$ on a valid frequency vector, meaning $f_{j,s}\ge0$ and $\sum_{j,s}f_{j,s}=1$. It returns $\rho$ when $f=p$. Some valid finite frequency vectors yield an output that is not positive semidefinite.

references.title: Xhek Turkeshi and Markus Heinrich, Quantum Information Methods for Many-Body Physics, §3.1
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §2.1.3
